back: Income is a flow of money per period (wages, rent, interest, benefits); wealth is a stock of assets owned at a point in time, less debts.
Inequality: 0 means perfect equality, 1 means one person has all the income; a higher value means more inequality.
A tax whose average rate rises as income rises.

front: How do you work out the average rate of income tax?
back: Tax paid ÷ income × 100; tax is calculated band by band at the marginal rates.

front: How is the quintile ratio found?
back: The income share of the richest 20% divided by the share of the poorest 20%.

front: List four causes of inequality of income and wealth.
back: Skills and education, ownership of assets, inheritance, discrimination or market power (also age and region).

front: List policies to redistribute income and wealth.
back: Progressive income taxes, transfer payments, a minimum wage, taxes on inheritance and capital, and state provision of essential goods and services.

front: What is the difference between universal and means-tested benefits?
back: Universal benefits go to everyone eligible by category; means-tested benefits go only to those below an income level, which costs less but is harder to administer.
High marginal tax rates and benefit withdrawal may reduce incentives to work, save and invest.
